events.text: In open court a god of {npc}'s rank rises and says, pleasantly, that your domain was theirs by right before you were named to it. {He} does not raise {his} voice. {He} has brought the old charters, in a case, with a ribbon.

effects.log: {npc} hands them over with a bow. They are real, and old, and, on one point, quite persuasive. You take them home.
You say the worshippers decide. {npc} smiles, and says that is exactly what {he} is counting on.

choices.text: Offer to share the first harvest

effects.log: {npc} declines, thoroughly, and is quietly rattled to have been offered.

events.text: At the turning of the offerings, you find another name beside yours at the altars of your own domain, a small one, in a fresh hand: {npc}. The mortals do not know why they feel obliged to light two lamps. They light two.

effects.log: You light it. {npc} comes to the altar that night, sees both lamps, and sits there for an hour, unable to be angry.
You snuff it. In the morning it is lit again, in a firmer hand, and {npc} is waiting politely for you.

choices.text: Leave a card on the altar

effects.log: You leave a card: "Welcome. Do not touch the left lamp." {npc} touches the left lamp, as a matter of principle.

events.text: {npc} arrives at the feast of the twelve domains with an entourage of seven minor gods and a speech about the "failure of the current stewardship of your domain". {He} looks directly at you. The speech takes three hours, and is very well made.

effects.log: You clap. The hall, startled, joins, and {npc}'s triumph tastes faintly of ash.
You rise and answer, point by point, and it is the best speech you have made in a thousand years, and {npc} listens to all of it.

choices.text: Ask for a copy of the speech

effects.log: {npc} sends one, annotated with objections to its own arguments. You find it very helpful.

events.text: The Book of Fates has a new note in the margin of your domain's page, in a hand that is not yours: "disputed", and a name. Fate does not choose sides, but it keeps good records. The name is {npc}'s, and {he} is standing at the next lectern, quill in hand.

choices.text: Add a note of your own

effects.log: You add "denied", in clean script. The book accepts it. {npc} accepts it too, with a short courteous nod, and the dispute begins in earnest.
"Your domain," says {npc}, "and a better ending than the last holder had." {He} says it kindly. It is the kindness that stings.
You strike it. It returns by morning. The Book appears to have opinions.

events.text: A drought of prayers has hit your domain's lowlands, and the farmers, in their trouble, have started to offer to {npc}, who stands just over the ridge of the sky. {He} has not asked for it. {He} has not refused it either.

effects.log: You send a sign, a small clean one, and the lowlands turn back to you in a night. {npc} bows from the ridge, to you, not the farmers.
{npc} refuses, with perfect grace, and the farmers are bewildered, and the dispute is born respectable.
You let them choose. They choose both, as mortals do, and the arrangement lasts a hundred years.

events.text: {npc} is a god of the Throne of Storms, and a hearing of the thunder-court has set the two of you side by side to argue the border of your domains. {He} argues in weather. By the third hour the chamber is raining, on {npc}'s side only.

effects.log: You answer with a clear sky, and the hall, which had been waiting for the clouds to break, breaks into applause.
You open an umbrella. A small, precise silence follows. Then the Throne laughs, and {npc} with it, wetly.
You argue back in dry facts. The rain on {npc}'s side lessens a little, which is the nearest thing to a concession.

events.text: There are two prayers for the same thing arriving at once, one addressed to you and one to {npc}, and the mortals who sent them are neighbours who have not spoken in forty years. Each is asking for the same rain. It is a very small drought.

effects.log: You give the rain to both fields at once, a fine soft one, and {npc} sees it come and sends a note: "Show-off."

choices.text: Give it to the one who prayed first

effects.log: You give it to the first. {npc} gives theirs to the second. The neighbours speak at last, to complain, and are friends by the harvest.
You let {npc} have the rain. {He} takes it, uncertain whether this is a gift or a game, and finds it, to {his} annoyance, both.

events.text: A new temple has gone up, grand and costly, to the glory of your domain, and its altar bears a god's face, but not yours. It is {npc}'s. The worshippers, it turns out, were told the temple was for "the lord of the domain", and did not ask which.

effects.log: You go in disguise. The priests are fervent and kind. You stay for the evening hymn and have to leave early, a little moved against your will.

choices.text: Send a larger gift to the temple

effects.log: You send a larger gift. {npc} accepts it for the temple, and sends a note of thanks, which is the most dangerous thing in the world.

choices.text: Ask the priests whose face it is

effects.log: You ask. They say, with perfect honesty, "The lord's." You understand how the thing was done, and admire it.

events.text: {npc} comes before you in the Silent Hall, where no one raises a voice, and says in a murmur that {he} intends to take your domain, and would like to do it correctly, with notice. {He} has brought a sealed card, to be read in a year, with {his} terms.

choices.text: Accept the card, and read it now

effects.log: You read it now. The terms are fair, and cold, and written in a hand that cost some effort to keep steady.

choices.text: Accept it, and wait the year

effects.log: You wait the year. It is the longest of your reign, and {npc} watches you wait, and is not entirely pleased with what it shows.
You hand it back. {npc} bows, and tucks it away, and the Hall carries the quiet away like a tray.

events.text: Somebody has painted your domain's sacred symbol with a line struck through it, on the wall of a minor shrine. Nobody has seen who. At dusk, {npc} appears at the shrine door and says: "That was not me. I would not do it so crudely. But I do know who did, and I will tell you for a price."

effects.log: "A conversation," says {npc}. "Every month for a year." You are astonished, and agree. The conversations are the oddest part of your century.
You refuse, and find out, with trouble, and the one who did it turns out to be a very junior god, who is forgiven in a sentence.

choices.text: Say you do not believe it was not {him}

effects.log: You say you do not believe it. {npc} says that is fair, and goes. The wall is repainted by someone, in the night, quite beautifully.

events.text: A procession of mortals is carrying a statue of {npc} up the long road to your shrine, to leave it at the door in a spirit of "fairness". The statue is badly carved. {npc} has been informed, and is hurrying after the procession, apologising to the mud.

effects.log: You receive the statue, and give it a corner. {npc} arrives, out of breath, to find you dusting it, and says nothing for a minute.
You send it back, with a flask of the shrine's wine. The mortals go home with a better story than they came with.
You help carry it, in disguise, up the last steep bit. {npc} glances at you, and at the statue, and the glance lasts a very long time.

events.text: Every god has a hall to which prayers are brought, and one night your hall and {npc}'s are connected by a broken wall. The first prayers come through to each side, and the two of you meet, in the dark, at the break, each holding a sheaf of the other's.

effects.log: You return them unread. {npc} does the same, and the pair of you stand there like thieves who have swapped loot and changed their minds.
You read one. It is a child, praying for a lost dog. You return it with a mark, and {npc} with a mark, and a dog is found.
You mend the wall together, with a brick each, in silence. It holds. The first spell of trust is a very small one.

events.text: At a sacrifice to your domain, the smoke goes up in the wrong direction: it bends toward {npc}'s mountain, and does not return. The priest looks at you in terror. {npc}, alone on the mountain, looks down at the smoke with an expression of purely embarrassed alarm.

choices.text: Send the smoke back with a breeze

effects.log: You send a breeze, and the smoke returns, and the priest weeps. {npc} sends a short message: "I did not do that. I wish I had thought of it."
You let it go, and walk to the mountain. {npc} is making tea. It is, by general agreement, the best argument for rivalry yet put.
You make a larger offering from your own stores, and the smoke goes straight up, and the priest says it is the most honest thing the sky has done for a year.

events.text: The gods of the Green Assembly hold their ancient trials of rivalry, in which two claimants to a domain grow a tree each from a seed, and the better tree decides. {npc} has put in a name for the trial. The Assembly sends you a seed, and a spade, and a most formal summons.

effects.log: You plant it with great care, and talk to it for a century. It grows crooked, and handsome, and the Assembly smiles.
You plant it beside theirs. In time the two trees grow around each other, and neither can be called better, and the Assembly sighs.

choices.text: Plant it in the dark of the moon

effects.log: You plant it in the dark of the moon, an old trick. It grows quickly, and badly, and tall, and {npc} looks on with sorrowful interest.

events.text: A hush falls over the Hall of Standings as a new name is read among the claimants to your domain: {npc}, a god who has ruled a lesser domain well for ages and now wants a greater. {He} walks the length of the Hall to bow to you, as protocol requires, and does not once look away.

effects.log: You return it exactly, to the hair. {npc} straightens, and something like respect crosses {his} face, and is put away at once.

choices.text: Ask what the lesser domain taught them

effects.log: "Patience," says {npc}, after a pause. "And the price of it." You file the answer, and are uneasy to find it useful.

choices.text: Offer the Hall a toast to the claimant

effects.log: You offer a toast. The Hall, thrown, drinks. {npc} drinks last, and slowly, and is plainly worried about you.

events.text: At the turning of an age, in the court of the gods, {npc} refers to your domain, in open court, as "the one that is nearly yours", and the court has the grace to look elsewhere. All the gods are looking at you to see how you take it.

choices.text: Answer with a line of your own

ok.log: Your answer is repeated all over by evening, and {npc} is not the one repeating it.

fail.log: Your answer lands a beat late, and {npc} thanks you for it, warmly.

effects.log: You bow to the last hair, and the silence is worth more than any speech you had ready.
You laugh, and for a moment {npc} looks as if something kind had struck them from behind.

events.text: On the night the worshippers lit the great fires far below, a drought strikes your domain, and {npc} sends rain, by the wrong road and with no note, so that no one can thank them. You owe them now, and both of you know it.

choices.text: Accept it, and say thank you properly

effects.log: You say thank you, in full form. {npc} goes stiff, then pink, and leaves in a dignified hurry.
You take the help and say nothing, and the nothing is understood, and is also, somehow, a debt of its own.
You refuse, politely, and {npc} goes away with the look of someone who has lost an argument they did not know they were in.

events.text: In a quiet corner of the Silent Hall, where no one is allowed to raise a voice, {npc} has laid a claim before the Silent Hall: that the northern rains were theirs before they were yours. The other gods are watching with a kind of bored interest.

ok.log: You take it, narrowly, and the Court talks of nothing else for a year.

fail.log: You lose it by a hair, and the hair is the thing everyone remembers.

effects.log: You withdraw with grace, and choose another field, and {npc} is left in possession of an empty victory.
You propose terms. {npc} reads them twice, and accepts three, and sends back a counter-proposal that is a work of art.

events.text: On the steps of the Will of Heaven, in full sight of everyone, a miracle you worked in the dry season is being preached, in the valley, as {npc}'s. The valley has no way of knowing. The record is dry, which is the worst of it.

effects.log: You correct it with sources, politely and in detail, and the correction is longer than the original, and read.

choices.text: Let it stand, and do better work

effects.log: You let it stand and do better work, and in time the work corrects the record on its own.

ok.log: {npc} admits it, in the end, in a voice that costs them a great deal, and offers a retraction.

fail.log: {npc} denies it with such grace that you almost believe it yourself.

events.text: Under a sky you had both made, and could not quite agree on, a tide comes up over the shrine-coast, and {npc} stands on the wall beside you, holding up the sea by sheer will. You are, for one night, simply on the same side.

choices.text: Hold your side with everything you have

ok.log: Your side holds, and so does theirs, and in the grey morning you are both still standing.

fail.log: Your side gives a little, and {npc} catches the slack without a word.

choices.text: Trust them with the dangerous half

effects.log: You hand {npc} the dangerous half, and they take it without a flicker, and it is the greatest compliment you have ever paid.

choices.text: Split the work by temper, not by rank

effects.log: You split it by temper. It is a raceter division than rank would have made, and the two of you are pleased in spite of yourselves.

events.text: In the cold light of a star that neither of you had made, you find {npc} alone on the old mountain at dusk, looking at the world below the way you do when you think nobody sees. It is the most honest hour of your acquaintance.

effects.log: You say the true thing, and {npc} stares at it as if it were a bird that had landed on the table.
You stay, and the silence is the answer, and the two of you are quiet until the lamps need trimming.
You make the joke, gently, and {npc} laughs, and the evening turns toward warmth.

events.text: At a convocation of domains called to discuss, supposedly, something else, Your oldest priestess has been seen leaving {npc}'s shrine with a bundle, and a look. You feel the ground move, if there were ground.

choices.text: Let them go, with a blessing

effects.log: You let them go, with a proper blessing, and the blessing is meant, and costs more than a refusal.

ok.log: You win them back with an offer that has nothing to do with money, and everything to do with remembering.

fail.log: You make the offer, and it is taken as an insult, and they leave faster.

effects.log: You turn up with a polite offer to one of {npc}'s best, and the dance of the long quarrel gains a new step.

events.text: At the edge of the divine realm, where the clouds are thinner and the prayers are louder, {npc} is raised in the court of the gods, and the lamps burned late on their mountain, and you could hear it from yours. Whatever the court says, the two of you know.

effects.log: You write a very short note, and it is sincere, and {npc} reads it a great many times.
You resolve to catch up, and the resolve lasts a decade, and works.
You do nothing, and feel all of it, and the feeling is a kind of work too.

events.text: In a hall of the Throne of Storms, where arguments are held in thunder, {npc} sends a very correct challenge in a very correct hand, on very expensive cloud, and the date is next week. Someone is already laying odds, and you will not look.

ok.log: You win it, narrowly, and the sound of the Court is a long, indrawn breath.

fail.log: You lose it, narrowly, and the sound of the Court is a long, indrawn breath.

effects.log: You postpone it a decade. They accept, with a tight, unreadable smile.
You offer a different test, of patience, of memory, of something less showy. They accept, and it is harder.

events.text: At the feast of the twelve domains, three thousand years into the dispute, {npc} arrives at a ritual in your honour and kindly blesses it on your behalf, in the old formula. You have been a god long enough to know when a barb is a barb.

choices.text: Ask a pointed question in return

effects.log: Your question is so reasonable that the answer takes a quarter of an hour, and {npc} is not the one who enjoys it.

choices.text: Let it pass, and note it

effects.log: You file it, as you file everything about {npc}, in the part of the memory that does not forget.

ok.log: The Court admires the return, and {npc} is quiet for a full day.

fail.log: The return is too sharp, and the room takes against the sharper of you.

events.text: In the Green Assembly's oldest grove, where the trees remember every oath, {npc} quietly stops a rumour from reaching the Silent Hall: that a flame of yours went out and was not relit. Neither of you refers to it again.

choices.text: Send back something of equal weight

effects.log: You return the favour exactly, to the ounce, and the exactness is the message.

choices.text: Say thanks in front of everyone

effects.log: You thank {npc} in public, which they hate, and which the Court is delighted by.

choices.text: Keep the debt and think about it

effects.log: You keep the debt in a drawer, and take it out on slow evenings, and turn it over.

events.text: In the hour when mortals bring their offerings and the gods pretend not to count, a shrine at a crossroads of two domains is receiving prayers, and both you and {npc} have turned up to claim them. You can hear the clouds thinking about it.

ok.log: You outwork them by a month, and the month decides it.

fail.log: You are outworked by a week, and the week stings more than a year would.

effects.log: You let them have it, and they know you let them, and it is the one thing they cannot forgive.

choices.text: Share it, if the rules allow

effects.log: The rules do not allow. You find a way. The result pleases nobody, and is remembered as fair.

events.text: At the funeral of a minor god, to which both of you were obliged to go, the Silent Hall's record of a great mercy now lists {npc} first and you second, in a very neat hand. You compose three replies and send none.

effects.log: Your version appears within the month, and it is clear, and plain, and hurries the matter along.

choices.text: Tell a friend and let it travel

effects.log: You tell one friend, and the story travels. By the next season, the truth has put its shoes on.
You say nothing. You remember. It is a long list, and it is getting tidy.

events.text: In the court of the gods, in the slow part of the afternoon, a mortal war, spiralling upward through prayers from both sides, will drag your domain and {npc}'s in unless the two of you hold the middle. No other god is watching, which is a relief and a loss.

choices.text: Say what must be said, plainly

effects.log: You say it plainly. {npc} says "Yes." The word is a whole treaty.

ok.log: The risk pays, by a thread, and {npc} looks at you across the wreckage with an entirely new expression.

fail.log: The risk costs you dearly, and {npc} pulls you out, and says nothing about it.

choices.text: Hold the line and let them lead

effects.log: You hold the line and let them lead. It is the hardest thing you have done in a century.

events.text: In the weeks after an unexpected miracle, whose credit was unclear, a message arrives from {npc}, brief and awkward, apologising for something done a thousand years ago in a tone that does not like apologising. You do not mention it afterwards, either of you.

effects.log: You give {npc} a small thing of yours. They look at it, then at you, then put it very carefully into a sleeve.
You ask a real question. The answer takes two cups of tea and a century, and is worth it.
You keep the distance. You are not sure you were wrong. You are not sure you were right.

events.text: When the prayers came in like weather, all from one side of the world, a patron god who funded your first age has been invited to dinner by {npc}. The invitation is on very good cloud. It is not theft. It is simply taking.

effects.log: You raise your own terms and your own manners, and the staff, noting both, stay.
You ask what was offered, and the answer is both humbler and kinder than you feared.

choices.text: Say nothing, and be a raceter host

effects.log: You say nothing, and become a better host, which is the only reply that lasts.

events.text: Between two harvests, in the lull when the faithful are too busy to pray, a thousand years of work at last pays for {npc}: a temple, a hymn, a following. The court applauds longer than seems necessary. It is a long time since anyone but them mattered this much.

effects.log: You go to the celebration, and bow, and are very good at it, and are carried home by your own dignity.
You send a modest gift, so modest that it becomes a statement, and {npc} does not know what to say.
You avoid the whole business, and find it follows you down the corridor anyway.

events.text: While a famine of belief moved across the lower lands, {npc} turns up at your shrine and begins to stretch, and asks if you have a minute, and the answer is not optional. You feel very old, and very young.

choices.text: Meet them on the first move

ok.log: You take the first move, and the second, and the Court sits up.

fail.log: They take the first move, and the second, and you are left explaining.

choices.text: Spar for form, not for stakes

effects.log: You spar for form, and the form is a pleasure, and neither of you will say so.
You decline, and say why, truthfully, and it is a surprise to both of you.

events.text: During a very long recess of the Book of Fates, {npc} has been telling the Silent Hall that your last miracle was "weather, mostly". The Hall is taking notes. The court is not sure whether to laugh.

choices.text: Take it as a compliment, loudly

effects.log: You thank them for the kind words, loudly, and {npc} has to carry the rest of the evening on those words.
You go home and work until the lamps burn low, and the work is better for the insult.
You answer by doing nothing, and doing it very well, and the room slowly leans your way.

events.text: A few centuries after the last time you had both said "never again", a heap of old, forgotten offerings arrives at your shrine from {npc}'s own, with a card saying "These were never mine". Gods have long memories, and this one will be kept.

effects.log: "Because it was correct," says {npc}, and then, after a long moment, "and because it was you."

choices.text: Do not ask, and be grateful

effects.log: You do not ask, and the not asking makes room for something that was not there before.
You suspect a trap and watch for a year. There is no trap. It stays with you more than a trap would have.

events.text: As the last of an age of worship burned down to its embers, a festival of the harvest has been scheduled for the same day in two valleys: one yours, one {npc}'s. You would rather win than be right.

effects.log: The arbiter hears you with the face of someone who has heard everything, and rules for neither, which is a victory of a sort.

choices.text: Win it in front of an audience

ok.log: You win it in full view, and the applause belongs, for once, to you.

fail.log: You lose it in full view, and the sound is of a great many people not saying anything.

effects.log: You concede, and ask a favour, and {npc} grants it before you finish asking. Neither of you quite knows what to do with this.

events.text: At the festival of the first sprouting, a priestess thanks {npc} for a harvest you ripened. They accept it graciously. You have the facts, and they have the room.

choices.text: Take it as a compliment to your work

effects.log: You take it as a compliment. The work was good enough to steal. It is a strange comfort.

choices.text: Demand an apology in open court

ok.log: The apology is made, in the end, and it is exactly as graceless as you had hoped.

fail.log: The demand is heard as pettiness, and the Court takes it out on you.

effects.log: You write the true account in the margins of three copies, in your own hand, and wait.

events.text: At the turning of an age, in the court of the gods, a star falls toward the lower lands, and {npc} turns to you and says, "You take the left." There will be no one to witness, and so it will matter.

choices.text: Stay with them to the end

effects.log: You stay to the end, and there is a grey dawn, and the two of you sit on the same step and do not talk.
You share the secret you have kept for a century, and the crisis passes, and the secret is not a secret any more.

choices.text: Take the credit later, and do the work now

effects.log: You do the work now. The credit can be argued about later, and is, with great relish.

events.text: On the night the worshippers lit the great fires far below, {npc} asks you, in the dark of the Silent Hall, whether the dispute has made either of you a better god. It sounds like a real question. For a moment the dispute is only an old habit.

choices.text: Take their hand, as a friend might

effects.log: You take their hand, briefly, and both of you recover with great dignity.
You say it. It is the first time you have said it aloud, and it is lighter than you thought.
You talk about swords until it is safe. Both of you are relieved, and a little disappointed.

events.text: In a quiet corner of the Silent Hall, where no one is allowed to raise a voice, {npc} has hired the one oracle on whom your plans depend, at a salary of faith the Court calls "indecent". Everyone is being scrupulously polite.

effects.log: You take it as a warning, and spend a decade tidying the cracks you had stopped looking at.
You confront {npc}, who is entirely unrepentant and entirely charming, and offers you a chair.

ok.log: You outbid them quietly, and the quiet is the best part of it.

fail.log: You outbid them, and the bid is a little too loud, and the Court hears.

events.text: On the steps of the Will of Heaven, in full sight of everyone, {npc} is given the sceptre of a domain you had hoped for, and sends a note by the sparrow-post that is, to your considerable irritation, gracious. It is a very quiet kind of war.

choices.text: Seize the moment and press the advantage

effects.log: You press the advantage, and for a season you are the one the Court looks at.

choices.text: Reach out, now, while it matters

effects.log: You reach out, now, when it would be easy not to, and it is accepted with a stiffness that is also gratitude.

choices.text: Say a prayer for them, privately

effects.log: You say a prayer for them, privately. You are surprised by how much you mean it.

events.text: Under a sky you had both made, and could not quite agree on, a friendly show of weather with {npc} over the sea becomes, by the third gust, something the lower lands stop to watch. It will settle nothing and matter completely.

ok.log: It is your best fight, and the one you will describe on the day you die.

fail.log: It is your best fight, and it is not enough, and it is better than most victories.

choices.text: Ask for a witness you trust

effects.log: You ask for a witness you trust, and the match is fair, and the result is accepted even by those who lose it.

choices.text: Make it a lesson, not a duel

effects.log: You turn the duel into a lesson, for yourself, and let them win the points while you win the thing under the points.

events.text: In the cold light of a star that neither of you had made, {npc} sends a gift to your shrine: a very small offering, correctly made, and a note saying "for the effort". You will remember this for a thousand years.

ok.log: Your quotation is from a book {npc} has not read, and they feel its edge for a year.

fail.log: Your quotation is from a book {npc} has, and has annotated.

choices.text: Compliment them back, a little too well

effects.log: You praise {npc} so thoroughly and so exactly that the praise itself becomes a kind of reproach.
You walk out without haste, and the talk follows you, and the dignity is the main topic.

events.text: At a convocation of domains called to discuss, supposedly, something else, {npc} speaks up for you in the court of the gods, briefly and with obvious distaste for having to. It changes nothing and everything.

choices.text: Pay it back at the first chance

effects.log: The first chance comes in four years, and you take it, and {npc} accepts it with the look of someone paid in the right coin.

choices.text: Offer a drink, as one equal to another

effects.log: You pour two cups. {npc} looks at theirs as if it might bite, and drinks it.

choices.text: Receive it, then beat them anyway

effects.log: You take the help, and the next time you face them, you win, and neither of you says a word of the other thing.

events.text: At the edge of the divine realm, where the clouds are thinner and the prayers are louder, {npc} proposes a contest of seasons: a year each of their weather and yours, and the worshippers to judge. It is a small thing and the stakes are everything.

choices.text: Prepare in silence for a decade

effects.log: You go quiet for ten years. When you come out, the field has changed, and so have you.
The note is friendly and perfectly unnerving, and {npc} loses a night's sleep over it.

ok.log: The surprise lands, and for once the cloud falls your way.

fail.log: The surprise falls flat, and so do you, a little.

events.text: In a hall of the Throne of Storms, where arguments are held in thunder, {npc} tells a story at the feast: a very good story, in which they play your part, and play it well. Faith is a slow court.

effects.log: You thank {npc} for the attention, so sweetly that it is reported as a threat, and so it is.
You publish something new, that cannot be misattributed, and say very little about the old.
You forgive it. The forgiving takes a year, not a moment, and leaves you lighter than a victory would.

effects.log: You wish them well, and mean it, and find that meaning it makes the loss lighter.

choices.text: Remind them of the old days

effects.log: You remind them of the old days. They look uncomfortable, and then moved, and then undecided.
You make a quiet list, in a book you do not show anyone, and the list has more names on it than you expected.

events.text: In the court of the gods, in the slow part of the afternoon, you and {npc} are both passed over for the same honour, and sit side by side in the ante-hall, looking at the same mural. The ladder only goes one way, and every god is on it.

effects.log: You take the lesson, which is a long one, and put it to work in the next decade.

choices.text: Make the most of the lull

effects.log: You make the most of the lull, and by its end you are quite a different person.

choices.text: Walk over and speak to them

effects.log: You walk over, and speak, and the speaking is the whole thing.

events.text: In the weeks after an unexpected miracle, whose credit was unclear, {npc} asks for a duel on the plain, at night, with the stars put out, "to see which of us is really seeing". The court is quieter than usual.

choices.text: Use the thing you have been hiding

ok.log: The hidden thing lands, and the Court gasps, and {npc} smiles, very slightly, delighted.

fail.log: The hidden thing is read as it lands, and answered, and {npc} smiles, very slightly, delighted.

choices.text: Hold the draw and call it fair

effects.log: You hold the draw, and call it fair, and the Court is both disappointed and relieved.
You withdraw with a bow, so full and strange that {npc} is the one left flustered.

events.text: When the prayers came in like weather, all from one side of the world, {npc} pays a long courtesy to your seat, and sits in it for a moment, as if testing the cushion. It was done beautifully, and that is the insult.

choices.text: Smile, and invite them to tea

effects.log: The invitation is accepted, to the horror of both parties, and the tea is long and strange.

choices.text: Leave a note on their desk

effects.log: You leave a note on {npc}'s desk, one line, and it is found, and it is not mentioned, and it is not forgotten.
You ignore it so completely that it begins to look like a decision, and then like a victory.

events.text: In a debate on the borders of domains, {npc} gives up a point, quietly, that would have sunk you. It is the most irritating mercy you have ever received.

choices.text: Admit, to yourself, that you misjudged

effects.log: You write it in your private book, and underline it, and do not look at it again.

choices.text: Tell the Court what they did

effects.log: You tell the Court, and the Court blinks, and {npc} never forgives you, quite, and never ceases to be grateful either.

choices.text: Say nothing at all, and nod

effects.log: You nod, once, across the room. It is a very small nod. It carries a very great deal.

events.text: While a famine of belief moved across the lower lands, {npc} asks the Green Assembly to rule on whether a river is yours or theirs. The river is considering. The faithful have taken sides.

effects.log: You step aside with a grace that is not entirely a performance, and a few watching are quite moved.

ok.log: You press, and the claim holds, and {npc} bows, which is new, and goes away to train, which is not.

fail.log: You press, and the claim does not hold, and your pride takes the blow.

effects.log: You ask the Court to decide. It takes a decade, and in that decade you each learn how well the other waits.

events.text: During a very long recess of the Book of Fates, a lesser god of your own court begins, unprompted, to explain the "dispute" in terms entirely favourable to {npc}. It is hard to be angry at a very accurate lie.

effects.log: You tell a better story, with fewer errors, and the room is moved in the other direction.
The witnesses speak. Two of them remember. One of them remembers wrongly, in {npc}'s favour.

choices.text: Take the lesson and keep the receipts

effects.log: You keep every receipt thereafter, and your records become the envy of the domains.

events.text: A few centuries after the last time you had both said "never again", a mountain of the Throne of Storms is slipping toward a valley of your faithful, and {npc} is already pushing back. The dispute will have to wait its turn.

choices.text: Take the front, without being asked

effects.log: You take the front. {npc} notes it, and does not argue, and later says only "You were always going to."

choices.text: Take the rear, and trust the front

effects.log: You take the rear, and trust, and the trust is the thing you will remember.

choices.text: Improvise, and ask them to follow

effects.log: You improvise, and {npc} follows, and the whole thing works, to the surprise of both.

events.text: As the last of an age of worship burned down to its embers, {npc} says in passing, in the hall of the Will of Heaven, that they are tired. Then they look horrified. The world below goes on being very large.

effects.log: You confess you envy them. {npc} says "Of course you do," and then, much more quietly, "And I you."

choices.text: Say you will not forget this

effects.log: You say you will not forget it, and you do not, and it comes up at the strangest times.

choices.text: Leave first, so they need not

effects.log: You leave first, so that they will not have to. It is the kindest thing you can think of, and they know.

events.text: On the mountain where the gods go when they want to be alone together, {npc} attends the wedding of your favourite hero, as a guest of honour, and makes a speech that is, annoyingly, wonderful. Loyalty among gods is a seasonal crop.

choices.text: Raise a toast to the departing

effects.log: You raise a toast, and the room, taken by surprise, joins in, and the departure becomes a feast.
You offer a better seat, and the seat, in the end, is the whole matter.

choices.text: Let the quarrel carry on elsewhere

effects.log: You let the quarrel carry on elsewhere, and discover you have a good deal more peace than you had thought.

events.text: At the turning of an age, in the court of the gods, {npc} has withdrawn to a long retreat in the hills. Their shrine is shuttered. You catch yourself walking by it. The scales tip, as scales do.

effects.log: You hold your head up, and the Court, noting it, adjusts its opinion.
You take a quiet year, and the year is exactly what you needed.

choices.text: Challenge them to measure the gap

effects.log: You challenge them to measure the gap, and the measurement, whatever it is, is the beginning of the next chapter.

events.text: On the night the worshippers lit the great fires far below, a miracle {npc} has built to beat you stands waiting. You can feel it across the court, polished, patient, rude. Both of you know the rules and neither is following them.

ok.log: You take it, and you hear it ring for a week, and it is not as sweet as you had planned.

fail.log: You lose it, and hear the sound of it for a week, and it is not as bitter as you had feared.

effects.log: You yield the field, which is a great deal harder than winning it, and everyone sees.

choices.text: Ask for a rematch at once

effects.log: You ask for a rematch at once. They are delighted, and appalled, and agree.

events.text: In a quiet corner of the Silent Hall, where no one is allowed to raise a voice, the Throne of Storms holds a feast and the seating puts you three places farther from the head than {npc}. All the gods are looking at you to see how you take it.

choices.text: Answer with a line of your own

ok.log: Your answer is repeated all over by evening, and {npc} is not the one repeating it.

fail.log: Your answer lands a beat late, and {npc} thanks you for it, warmly.

effects.log: You bow to the last hair, and the silence is worth more than any speech you had ready.
You laugh, and for a moment {npc} looks as if something kind had struck them from behind.

events.text: On the steps of the Will of Heaven, in full sight of everyone, {npc} calls a truce for a season, when your shrines are low, and keeps it so well that you begin to suspect them of enjoying it. You owe them now, and both of you know it.

choices.text: Accept it, and say thank you properly

effects.log: You say thank you, in full form. {npc} goes stiff, then pink, and leaves in a dignified hurry.
You take the help and say nothing, and the nothing is understood, and is also, somehow, a debt of its own.
You refuse, politely, and {npc} goes away with the look of someone who has lost an argument they did not know they were in.

events.text: Under a sky you had both made, and could not quite agree on, a hero of the lower world is sworn to both of you, and now must choose a banner. {npc} sent a very nice one. The other gods are watching with a kind of bored interest.

ok.log: You take it, narrowly, and the Court talks of nothing else for a year.

fail.log: You lose it by a hair, and the hair is the thing everyone remembers.

effects.log: You withdraw with grace, and choose another field, and {npc} is left in possession of an empty victory.
You propose terms. {npc} reads them twice, and accepts three, and sends back a counter-proposal that is a work of art.

events.text: In the cold light of a star that neither of you had made, a book of the Book of Fates, still wet, records the deed of the age, and gives {npc} a share of it that is slightly wrong. The record is dry, which is the worst of it.

effects.log: You correct it with sources, politely and in detail, and the correction is longer than the original, and read.

choices.text: Let it stand, and do better work

effects.log: You let it stand and do better work, and in time the work corrects the record on its own.

ok.log: {npc} admits it, in the end, in a voice that costs them a great deal, and offers a retraction.

fail.log: {npc} denies it with such grace that you almost believe it yourself.

events.text: At a convocation of domains called to discuss, supposedly, something else, a very old demon of hunger approaches the harvest-lands. You and {npc} meet at the edge of the fields, unarmed, and exchange a nod. You are, for one night, simply on the same side.

choices.text: Hold your side with everything you have

ok.log: Your side holds, and so does theirs, and in the grey morning you are both still standing.

fail.log: Your side gives a little, and {npc} catches the slack without a word.

choices.text: Trust them with the dangerous half

effects.log: You hand {npc} the dangerous half, and they take it without a flicker, and it is the greatest compliment you have ever paid.

choices.text: Split the work by temper, not by rank

effects.log: You split it by temper. It is a raceter division than rank would have made, and the two of you are pleased in spite of yourselves.

events.text: At the edge of the divine realm, where the clouds are thinner and the prayers are louder, {npc} asks you to teach them just one thing: what you do before a hard prayer is answered. It is the most honest hour of your acquaintance.

effects.log: You say the true thing, and {npc} stares at it as if it were a bird that had landed on the table.
You stay, and the silence is the answer, and the two of you are quiet until the lamps need trimming.
You make the joke, gently, and {npc} laughs, and the evening turns toward warmth.

choices.text: Let them go, with a blessing

effects.log: You let them go, with a proper blessing, and the blessing is meant, and costs more than a refusal.

ok.log: You win them back with an offer that has nothing to do with money, and everything to do with remembering.

fail.log: You make the offer, and it is taken as an insult, and they leave faster.

effects.log: You turn up with a polite offer to one of {npc}'s best, and the dance of the long quarrel gains a new step.

events.text: At the feast of the twelve domains, three thousand years into the dispute, the court names a new god "the pride of the heavens", and it is neither of you. You and {npc} meet by accident, afterwards, in the garden. Whatever the court says, the two of you know.

effects.log: You write a very short note, and it is sincere, and {npc} reads it a great many times.
You resolve to catch up, and the resolve lasts a decade, and works.
You do nothing, and feel all of it, and the feeling is a kind of work too.

events.text: In the Green Assembly's oldest grove, where the trees remember every oath, {npc} arrives with a new weapon and an old grudge and says they are tired of being polite about either. Someone is already laying odds, and you will not look.

ok.log: You win it, narrowly, and the sound of the Court is a long, indrawn breath.

fail.log: You lose it, narrowly, and the sound of the Court is a long, indrawn breath.

effects.log: You postpone it a decade. They accept, with a tight, unreadable smile.
You offer a different test, of patience, of memory, of something less showy. They accept, and it is harder.

events.text: In the hour when mortals bring their offerings and the gods pretend not to count, {npc} repeats a prayer meant for you, aloud, in a slightly better voice. You have been a god long enough to know when a barb is a barb.

choices.text: Ask a pointed question in return

effects.log: Your question is so reasonable that the answer takes a quarter of an hour, and {npc} is not the one who enjoys it.

choices.text: Let it pass, and note it

effects.log: You file it, as you file everything about {npc}, in the part of the memory that does not forget.

ok.log: The Court admires the return, and {npc} is quiet for a full day.

fail.log: The return is too sharp, and the room takes against the sharper of you.

events.text: At the funeral of a minor god, to which both of you were obliged to go, {npc} sends a god of the dead to speak for one of your faithful, who would otherwise have been forgotten. Neither of you refers to it again.

choices.text: Send back something of equal weight

effects.log: You return the favour exactly, to the ounce, and the exactness is the message.

choices.text: Say thanks in front of everyone

effects.log: You thank {npc} in public, which they hate, and which the Court is delighted by.

choices.text: Keep the debt and think about it

effects.log: You keep the debt in a drawer, and take it out on slow evenings, and turn it over.

events.text: In the court of the gods, in the slow part of the afternoon, a dream was sent to a mortal king and signed by you and {npc}. Neither of you sent it. One of you is lying. You can hear the clouds thinking about it.

ok.log: You outwork them by a month, and the month decides it.

fail.log: You are outworked by a week, and the week stings more than a year would.

effects.log: You let them have it, and they know you let them, and it is the one thing they cannot forgive.

choices.text: Share it, if the rules allow

effects.log: The rules do not allow. You find a way. The result pleases nobody, and is remembered as fair.

events.text: In the weeks after an unexpected miracle, whose credit was unclear, you find a small altar to {npc} in a village you saved from a flood. They are very happy there. You compose three replies and send none.

effects.log: Your version appears within the month, and it is clear, and plain, and hurries the matter along.

choices.text: Tell a friend and let it travel

effects.log: You tell one friend, and the story travels. By the next season, the truth has put its shoes on.
You say nothing. You remember. It is a long list, and it is getting tidy.

events.text: When the prayers came in like weather, all from one side of the world, a burst of heavenly fire, from a quarrel not yours, comes down over a village that prays to you and {npc} both. No other god is watching, which is a relief and a loss.

choices.text: Say what must be said, plainly

effects.log: You say it plainly. {npc} says "Yes." The word is a whole treaty.

ok.log: The risk pays, by a thread, and {npc} looks at you across the wreckage with an entirely new expression.

fail.log: The risk costs you dearly, and {npc} pulls you out, and says nothing about it.

choices.text: Hold the line and let them lead

effects.log: You hold the line and let them lead. It is the hardest thing you have done in a century.

events.text: Between two harvests, in the lull when the faithful are too busy to pray, you walk home by the same road, and {npc} walks a pace behind, out of habit, and says nothing the whole way. You do not mention it afterwards, either of you.

effects.log: You give {npc} a small thing of yours. They look at it, then at you, then put it very carefully into a sleeve.
You ask a real question. The answer takes two cups of tea and a century, and is worth it.
You keep the distance. You are not sure you were wrong. You are not sure you were right.

events.text: While a famine of belief moved across the lower lands, a god you both would agree to dislike has been offered a place at {npc}'s table, and has accepted. It is not theft. It is simply taking.

effects.log: You raise your own terms and your own manners, and the staff, noting both, stay.
You ask what was offered, and the answer is both humbler and kinder than you feared.

choices.text: Say nothing, and be a raceter host

effects.log: You say nothing, and become a better host, which is the only reply that lasts.

events.text: During a very long recess of the Book of Fates, {npc} announces a very long vigil, a thousand years, to perfect a miracle. It is clearly aimed at you, and quite sincere. It is a long time since anyone but them mattered this much.

effects.log: You go to the celebration, and bow, and are very good at it, and are carried home by your own dignity.
You send a modest gift, so modest that it becomes a statement, and {npc} does not know what to say.
You avoid the whole business, and find it follows you down the corridor anyway.

events.text: A few centuries after the last time you had both said "never again", you and {npc} are told to settle your quarrel the old way before the court takes sides. The old way is a storm, a sword, and a bow. You feel very old, and very young.

choices.text: Meet them on the first move

ok.log: You take the first move, and the second, and the Court sits up.

fail.log: They take the first move, and the second, and you are left explaining.

choices.text: Spar for form, not for stakes

effects.log: You spar for form, and the form is a pleasure, and neither of you will say so.
You decline, and say why, truthfully, and it is a surprise to both of you.

events.text: As the last of an age of worship burned down to its embers, {npc} publicly hopes that your temple's roof is "holding up". It is the one thing it is not doing. The court is not sure whether to laugh.

choices.text: Take it as a compliment, loudly

effects.log: You thank them for the kind words, loudly, and {npc} has to carry the rest of the evening on those words.
You go home and work until the lamps burn low, and the work is better for the insult.
You answer by doing nothing, and doing it very well, and the room slowly leans your way.

events.text: On the mountain where the gods go when they want to be alone together, {npc} arrives at your hour of need with the right miracle, and looks at it as if it had been inconveniently correct. Gods have long memories, and this one will be kept.

effects.log: "Because it was correct," says {npc}, and then, after a long moment, "and because it was you."

choices.text: Do not ask, and be grateful

effects.log: You do not ask, and the not asking makes room for something that was not there before.
You suspect a trap and watch for a year. There is no trap. It stays with you more than a trap would have.

events.text: At the turning of an age, in the court of the gods, a great oracle has declared, in double meaning, that one of you will outlast the other. {npc} is already reading it as a promise. You would rather win than be right.

effects.log: The arbiter hears you with the face of someone who has heard everything, and rules for neither, which is a victory of a sort.

choices.text: Win it in front of an audience

ok.log: You win it in full view, and the applause belongs, for once, to you.

fail.log: You lose it in full view, and the sound is of a great many people not saying anything.

effects.log: You concede, and ask a favour, and {npc} grants it before you finish asking. Neither of you quite knows what to do with this.

events.text: On the night the worshippers lit the great fires far below, {npc} accepts a crown of flowers at a spring festival, and the flowers were grown by your faithful. You have the facts, and they have the room.

choices.text: Take it as a compliment to your work

effects.log: You take it as a compliment. The work was good enough to steal. It is a strange comfort.

choices.text: Demand an apology in open court

ok.log: The apology is made, in the end, and it is exactly as graceless as you had hoped.

fail.log: The demand is heard as pettiness, and the Court takes it out on you.

effects.log: You write the true account in the margins of three copies, in your own hand, and wait.

events.text: In a quiet corner of the Silent Hall, where no one is allowed to raise a voice, a child god, newly born, has been abandoned on the threshold of the Silent Hall, and {npc} found them first, and looks at you. There will be no one to witness, and so it will matter.

choices.text: Stay with them to the end

effects.log: You stay to the end, and there is a grey dawn, and the two of you sit on the same step and do not talk.
You share the secret you have kept for a century, and the crisis passes, and the secret is not a secret any more.

choices.text: Take the credit later, and do the work now

effects.log: You do the work now. The credit can be argued about later, and is, with great relish.

events.text: On the steps of the Will of Heaven, in full sight of everyone, an old hymn comes up from the lower lands on the wind, and {npc} hums it, and then stops, caught. For a moment the dispute is only an old habit.

choices.text: Take their hand, as a friend might

effects.log: You take their hand, briefly, and both of you recover with great dignity.
You say it. It is the first time you have said it aloud, and it is lighter than you thought.
You talk about swords until it is safe. Both of you are relieved, and a little disappointed.

events.text: Under a sky you had both made, and could not quite agree on, the weaver of the gods' robes has made a new one in {npc}'s hues, and pointedly thanked you for the "inspiration". Everyone is being scrupulously polite.

effects.log: You take it as a warning, and spend a decade tidying the cracks you had stopped looking at.
You confront {npc}, who is entirely unrepentant and entirely charming, and offers you a chair.

ok.log: You outbid them quietly, and the quiet is the best part of it.

fail.log: You outbid them, and the bid is a little too loud, and the Court hears.

events.text: In the cold light of a star that neither of you had made, you come into a great miracle, and for one evening you are far ahead. {npc} arrives, unannounced, with wine, and says only "Show me". It is a very quiet kind of war.

choices.text: Seize the moment and press the advantage

effects.log: You press the advantage, and for a season you are the one the Court looks at.

choices.text: Reach out, now, while it matters

effects.log: You reach out, now, when it would be easy not to, and it is accepted with a stiffness that is also gratitude.

choices.text: Say a prayer for them, privately

effects.log: You say a prayer for them, privately. You are surprised by how much you mean it.

events.text: At a convocation of domains called to discuss, supposedly, something else, you and {npc} are arranged, by ministerial ill-humour, to open a festival with a match. The audience has brought food. It will settle nothing and matter completely.

ok.log: It is your best fight, and the one you will describe on the day you die.

fail.log: It is your best fight, and it is not enough, and it is better than most victories.

choices.text: Ask for a witness you trust

effects.log: You ask for a witness you trust, and the match is fair, and the result is accepted even by those who lose it.

choices.text: Make it a lesson, not a duel

effects.log: You turn the duel into a lesson, for yourself, and let them win the points while you win the thing under the points.

events.text: At the edge of the divine realm, where the clouds are thinner and the prayers are louder, {npc} sends a very neat set of corrections to your last decree, with a little red mark beside each. You will remember this for a thousand years.

ok.log: Your quotation is from a book {npc} has not read, and they feel its edge for a year.

fail.log: Your quotation is from a book {npc} has, and has annotated.

choices.text: Compliment them back, a little too well

effects.log: You praise {npc} so thoroughly and so exactly that the praise itself becomes a kind of reproach.
You walk out without haste, and the talk follows you, and the dignity is the main topic.

events.text: In a hall of the Throne of Storms, where arguments are held in thunder, a letter of thanks from one of your lesser gods, who was spared a quarrel, bears {npc}'s hand in the margin. It changes nothing and everything.

choices.text: Pay it back at the first chance

effects.log: The first chance comes in four years, and you take it, and {npc} accepts it with the look of someone paid in the right coin.

choices.text: Offer a drink, as one equal to another

effects.log: You pour two cups. {npc} looks at theirs as if it might bite, and drinks it.

choices.text: Receive it, then beat them anyway

effects.log: You take the help, and the next time you face them, you win, and neither of you says a word of the other thing.

events.text: At the feast of the twelve domains, three thousand years into the dispute, a cairn of offerings on a border-mountain has grown so high that it is claimed by you and {npc} both, and by the mountain. It is a small thing and the stakes are everything.

choices.text: Prepare in silence for a decade

effects.log: You go quiet for ten years. When you come out, the field has changed, and so have you.
The note is friendly and perfectly unnerving, and {npc} loses a night's sleep over it.

ok.log: The surprise lands, and for once the cloud falls your way.

fail.log: The surprise falls flat, and so do you, a little.

events.text: In the Green Assembly's oldest grove, where the trees remember every oath, the court turns to you, expecting a speech on a victory of yours, and {npc} has already begun one on your behalf. Faith is a slow court.

effects.log: You thank {npc} for the attention, so sweetly that it is reported as a threat, and so it is.
You publish something new, that cannot be misattributed, and say very little about the old.
You forgive it. The forgiving takes a year, not a moment, and leaves you lighter than a victory would.

events.text: In the hour when mortals bring their offerings and the gods pretend not to count, a rebellion of the minor gods is gathering at your border, and {npc} is gathering the other side, and has sent word to meet. Whatever happens, it will not be spoken of afterward.

ok.log: Together, you are better than either alone, and you both pretend not to notice.

fail.log: Together, you are not enough, and you both know it, and neither says so.

choices.text: Hold back, and watch what they do

effects.log: You hold back and watch. What they do tells you everything about them, and you are rather ashamed of the watching.
You call for everyone, and everyone comes, and the crisis becomes a quarrel about who came first.

events.text: At the funeral of a minor god, to which both of you were obliged to go, {npc} shows you, without a word, a scar from a quarrel in the first age, and the date. It has healed very neatly. You notice you are not angry.

effects.log: You offer to practise together. They hesitate for nine hundred years, and say yes.
You offer nothing, but remember, and the memory becomes a warmth you do not deserve and keep anyway.

choices.text: Tell them they were right once

effects.log: You tell {npc} they were right, once, about something long ago. They are quiet for a very long time.

events.text: In the court of the gods, in the slow part of the afternoon, the old keeper of your temple's flame is retiring to {npc}'s domain, with a pension. You have your own habits to blame.

choices.text: Wish them well and mean it

effects.log: You wish them well, and mean it, and find that meaning it makes the loss lighter.

choices.text: Remind them of the old days

effects.log: You remind them of the old days. They look uncomfortable, and then moved, and then undecided.
You make a quiet list, in a book you do not show anyone, and the list has more names on it than you expected.

events.text: In the weeks after an unexpected miracle, whose credit was unclear, the first time in an age that {npc} is truly ahead of you, they say nothing. They simply stand a little taller. The ladder only goes one way, and every god is on it.

effects.log: You take the lesson, which is a long one, and put it to work in the next decade.

choices.text: Make the most of the lull

effects.log: You make the most of the lull, and by its end you are quite a different person.

choices.text: Walk over and speak to them

effects.log: You walk over, and speak, and the speaking is the whole thing.

events.text: When the prayers came in like weather, all from one side of the world, {npc} asks the Silent Hall to clear the room for a duel of dreams, and says only: "I want to see what you are when you lose. Nobody has ever shown me." The court is quieter than usual.

ok.log: The hidden thing lands, and the Court gasps, and {npc} smiles, very slightly, delighted.

fail.log: The hidden thing is read as it lands, and answered, and {npc} smiles, very slightly, delighted.

choices.text: Hold the draw and call it fair

effects.log: You hold the draw, and call it fair, and the Court is both disappointed and relieved.
You withdraw with a bow, so full and strange that {npc} is the one left flustered.

events.text: Between two harvests, in the lull when the faithful are too busy to pray, {npc} has had the temple choir learn a hymn in which a god "of modest gifts" is praised for patience. The god is not named. The choir does not look at you, which is how you know. It was done beautifully, and that is the insult.

choices.text: Smile, and invite them to tea

effects.log: The invitation is accepted, to the horror of both parties, and the tea is long and strange.

choices.text: Leave a note on their desk

effects.log: You leave a note on {npc}'s desk, one line, and it is found, and it is not mentioned, and it is not forgotten.
You ignore it so completely that it begins to look like a decision, and then like a victory.

events.text: While a famine of belief moved across the lower lands, Your shrine on the northern pass has been dug out of the snow overnight by unseen hands, and the path sanded. The only mark is a single frosted footprint of a very particular boot, which you know from the court. It is the most irritating mercy you have ever received.

choices.text: Admit, to yourself, that you misjudged

effects.log: You write it in your private book, and underline it, and do not look at it again.

choices.text: Tell the Court what they did

effects.log: You tell the Court, and the Court blinks, and {npc} never forgives you, quite, and never ceases to be grateful either.

choices.text: Say nothing at all, and nod

effects.log: You nod, once, across the room. It is a very small nod. It carries a very great deal.

events.text: During a very long recess of the Book of Fates, {npc} has laid a stake at the feast of the Thunder God that their harvest bells will outsound yours across the valley. The Thunder God is the judge, already drunk, and has promised to listen fairly. The faithful have taken sides.

effects.log: You step aside with a grace that is not entirely a performance, and a few watching are quite moved.

ok.log: You press, and the claim holds, and {npc} bows, which is new, and goes away to train, which is not.

fail.log: You press, and the claim does not hold, and your pride takes the blow.

effects.log: You ask the Court to decide. It takes a decade, and in that decade you each learn how well the other waits.

events.text: A few centuries after the last time you had both said "never again", a scribe of the Silent Hall, copying the year's memorials, enters {npc} as "the sender of the rains", which you sent. The scribe is very apologetic, and the ink is already dry, and the Hall does not strike things. It is hard to be angry at a very accurate lie.

effects.log: You tell a better story, with fewer errors, and the room is moved in the other direction.
The witnesses speak. Two of them remember. One of them remembers wrongly, in {npc}'s favour.

choices.text: Take the lesson and keep the receipts

effects.log: You keep every receipt thereafter, and your records become the envy of the domains.

events.text: You have beaten {npc} before half a pantheon three times, and the court has stopped guessing at a fourth. {npc} comes to your altar with nothing in {his} hands and says: "My claim is thin. I can drag it out for an age. Or I can end it. Which would you rather?"

effects.log: {npc} is silent. Then {he} says "Good", in the voice of a god who has been holding a long breath.

choices.text: End it, and let the claim lapse

effects.log: You accept the lapse. {npc} nods, and walks out into the evening, and the matter has an ending but not a warmth.
You say share. {npc} thinks about it for nine centuries and says yes, to the first half.

events.text: The third defeat is witnessed by the Throne of Storms, who ordinarily approve of nothing. {npc} bows, and says in the old formula that {he} withdraws the claim. The court exhales. Afterwards, in the corridor, {he} says, quietly, "Come and eat. I cook badly."

effects.log: You go and eat. The cooking is terrible. You say so. {npc} laughs until the table shakes.
You decline, with thanks. {npc} nods, and the dinner is not had. A certain door is closed, softly.
You bring your own dish. {npc} samples it, and says it is worse than {his} own, and takes a second helping.

events.text: {npc} sends a message by a humble prayer-angel: "Three times. I concede the domain, the argument, and the dispute. I would like one thing from you, and it is a small one: that my name stay in the book beside yours, as a claimant who lost well."

effects.log: You grant it. In the Book of Fates a small line is added, and the margin, for once, is warm.

choices.text: Grant it, and add a line

effects.log: You grant it and add a line: "who also held the field." The Book accepts the line without comment.

choices.text: Say the book is not yours to give

effects.log: You say the book is not yours to give. {npc} accepts that, and the claim ends, and the name is left to Fate.

events.text: When you win the third time, {npc} laughs, and keeps laughing, a deep, rolling thunder of a laugh, until the lamps rattle. "I have been so tired of this," {he} says. "You have no idea. Thank you." {He} wipes {his} eyes with a sleeve of cloud.

effects.log: You laugh with them. It rolls over the lower lands, and a farmer, far below, looks up and says it is going to be a good season.

choices.text: Ask what they will do now

effects.log: "Sleep," says {npc}. "For about a century." {He} yawns, hugely, and the lamps flicker.

choices.text: Offer them a place at your altar

effects.log: You offer a place at your altar. {npc} says it is the nicest insult anyone has paid {him}, and accepts.

events.text: The third defeat, in front of the Silent Hall, is unremarked: the Hall does not applaud and does not sigh. {npc} stands, bows, and in the great silence says, aloud, "I am finished." It is the loudest sentence ever spoken in that room.

choices.text: Bow in return, and say nothing

effects.log: You bow in return, and say nothing, and the Hall remembers the quiet for ten thousand years.

choices.text: Walk across the Hall to them

effects.log: You walk across. It is a very long Hall. When you arrive, {npc} puts out a hand, and you take it, and the Hall remembers that instead.
You say it. {npc} nods slowly, and turns it over, and finds it good.

events.text: {npc} brings you the oldest charter of your domain, the one {he} had always claimed, and sets it on your altar. "It is yours," {he} says. "It always was. I kept it too long out of habit. I would like to stop being a god who keeps other gods' papers."

choices.text: Accept it, and read it aloud

effects.log: You read it aloud, in the old tongue, and {npc} listens with closed eyes. It is a very short charter, and a very old one.
You burn it on the altar. The smoke goes up straight. {npc} watches it go, and breathes out, long and thin.

choices.text: Give it back to them to keep

effects.log: You give it back. {npc} protests, and keeps it, and puts it in a place of honour, and says it is now a gift.

events.text: A bell tolls in the Silent Hall, which has no bell, and when you look up {npc} is standing at your elbow, apologising. "That was me," {he} says. "I have decided to end it, and I felt it needed a sound." The claim is closed by a bell that does not exist.

choices.text: Say it was a fine sound

effects.log: You say it was a fine sound. {npc} blushes, and the bell tolls once more, very softly, to thank you.

choices.text: Ask them to ring it again

effects.log: You ask. {npc} rings it again, and again, and you both stand there listening to a bell that is nowhere.

choices.text: Say you did not hear it

effects.log: You say you did not hear it. {npc} nods, and does not ring again, and the claim goes on being ended without a sound.

events.text: {npc} sits down at the foot of your altar after the third defeat, in the posture of a mortal at prayer, which is a thing a god does only with great intention. "I wished to see what it looks like from here," {he} says. "From where they pray."

effects.log: You sit with them. From the foot of the altar you see the whole long climb of the worshippers, and neither of you has anything to say, and it is the best conversation of the age.
"A very tall god, and a very small hope," says {npc}. "It is a sad view and a good one." You file it, and do not forget.
You leave them to it. When {he} rises, the claim is gone from {his} face, and the domain is yours without a word more said.

effects.log: You thank {him}. {npc} says honesty is the only luxury {he} has left, and the two of you go out together to look at the harvest.

choices.text: Ask what would have been worse

effects.log: "A god who asked for no rival," says {npc}. The line stays in the court as a proverb.

events.text: {npc} visits your domain as a pilgrim, in plain robes, to see what it is that {he} lost to. {He} walks the whole road with the worshippers, and kneels at your altar, and rises, and says to you, "Very well. I see it. I would have built it differently. I should have built it worse."

choices.text: Say that you would have built it worse, too

You pour for {him}. It is an old, small kindness, and in the Divine Realm there is nothing larger.

choices.text: Sit, and let it rest a while

effects.log: You sit on the step beside {npc}. The marble is cool. For a moment the long argument is only a long afternoon.

events.text: {npc} has your sword, or a god's version of it, and the grip is worn to the exact shape of your hand. "I picked it up in a battlefield I do not remember," {he} says. "It seemed to belong to someone I knew."

ok.log: You take it, and for the first time in several lives, the old pattern breaks, and falls your way.

fail.log: You take it, and the old pattern holds, and you hear a faint sound like a lock turning.

ok.log: You answer lightly, and {npc} cannot find the heavy reply, and laughs, defeated by a joke.

fail.log: You answer lightly, and {npc} answers lightly, and somehow you lose the exchange, and are fond of it.

choices.text: Walk on, and let them follow

effects.log: You walk on. After a moment you hear {npc}'s step behind yours, steady, a pace back. It is a comfort.

events.text: {npc} comes to you in the hour before dawn, when the lamps are low, and sits at your altar without being invited. "Whatever the old stories say," {he} says, "I would like to try a different ending."

ok.log: You fight clean, and win it, and {npc} says "Better," and means it.

fail.log: You fight clean, and {npc} fights cleaner, and you lose well, which is something.

ok.log: You out-think them, for once, by a small margin, and the Hall is silent in the way of a great many gods not saying anything.

fail.log: You try to out-think them, and every thought was theirs first.

choices.text: Ask what the last life was like

effects.log: {npc} tells you. It takes the night, and by the end you are not sure whether it was theirs or yours.

events.text: You and {npc} are the last two in the court after a long audience, and {he} sits on a step and says, "I am so tired of winning and losing to you. Would you sit?"

ok.log: You take the duel, and the Hall is silent, and the result is a thing both of you will remember into the next life.

fail.log: You take the duel, and it goes the way the old stories said, and you leave the Hall a little lighter and a little worse.

fail.log: You match wits, and {npc} knows you too well, and the wit of an old life is theirs.

effects.log: You sit on the step beside {npc}. The marble is cool. For a moment the long argument is only a long afternoon.

events.text: {npc} offers a race, an old joke between you in some other life: a single prayer, for the first to the next hearth. You do not remember the joke. You find that you are already moving.

ok.log: You take it, and for the first time in several lives, the old pattern breaks, and falls your way.

fail.log: You take it, and the old pattern holds, and you hear a faint sound like a lock turning.

events.text: {npc} asks whether you think souls are knotted by chance. You say you do not know. {He} says, "I used to think it was a punishment. Now I think it is a rope. I do not know whether to cut it."

ok.log: You fight clean, and win it, and {npc} says "Better," and means it.

fail.log: You fight clean, and {npc} fights cleaner, and you lose well, which is something.

effects.log: {npc} tells you. It takes the night, and by the end you are not sure whether it was theirs or yours.

events.text: {npc} has been ill, and does not say so, and you hear of it from three gods who each ask you not to mention it. You go. {He} receives you in a dressing gown of cloud, with great dignity.

ok.log: You take the duel, and the Hall is silent, and the result is a thing both of you will remember into the next life.

fail.log: You take the duel, and it goes the way the old stories said, and you leave the Hall a little lighter and a little worse.

fail.log: You match wits, and {npc} knows you too well, and the wit of an old life is theirs.

choices.text: Sit, and let it rest a while

effects.log: You sit on the step beside {npc}. The marble is cool. For a moment the long argument is only a long afternoon.

events.text: {npc} comes to the temple that was raised to both of you, in some lost age, by a farmer who could not decide, and stands at the altar that has two names carved into it, one worn almost smooth. "I think mine is the worn one," {he} says. "I think it was always going to be."

ok.log: You take the smooth name, and the stone warms, and a priestess who has prayed there for decades falls to the ground. {npc} looks relieved.

fail.log: You take the smooth name and are wrong; the worn one was yours. {npc} touches it gently, as if apologising to the stone.

effects.log: You pour a libation over both names, wine and rain, and stay until the candles go out.

events.text: A thunderstorm breaks over the lower lands, one of the Throne of Storms' old arguments, and {npc} stands in the middle of the clouds beside you, drenched, and says, "I used to be afraid of this. I do not know why I am not."

ok.log: You call down the lightning, and it comes, and the clouds part, and {npc} laughs aloud as the sun breaks through at your feet.

fail.log: You call down the lightning and it comes, but wrong, and strikes a hill; {npc} puts out the fire for you with one wave and says nothing kind.

effects.log: You hold your sleeve over {npc}'s head, absurdly, against a storm. They let you.

events.text: The prayers of a village below name you both in the same breath, as the God of the Well and the God of the Gate, and the villagers are fighting over which comes first in the grace. A child has written a petition: "Please make them stop."

ok.log: You answer the child before the elders, with a small miracle of calm, and the village obeys it for a season. {npc} follows with another.

fail.log: You answer the child with a miracle that goes slightly wrong, a swarm of harmless bees, and {npc} has to clean it up and says so.

effects.log: You and {npc} agree on a grace that names both gods in the order of the week. The village is satisfied and the child is promoted to priest.

events.text: The Silent Hall hears a case between two lesser gods and, reading the old record, finds that you and {npc} are named as witnesses on opposite sides. The Hall cannot rule until both have spoken. {npc} sits down across from you in the dock.

ok.log: You give your testimony plainly, and every detail matches the record. The Hall rules in favour of your side, and {npc} bows.

fail.log: You give your testimony and a detail, a date, is wrong. {npc}'s version stands, and the Hall is solemn and kind.

effects.log: You withdraw your testimony in favour of {npc}'s. The Hall is not used to it, and takes an hour to decide whether it is allowed.

events.text: A harvest festival is held in your honour in the valleys, and {npc} has sent, anonymously, a field of blue corn that was one of the old gifts of the Green Assembly. The corn is ripening overnight, rustling, enough for a hundred years.

choices.text: Take the corn to the valleys yourself

ok.log: You carry the corn to the valleys yourself, and the people eat, and thank you by name; {npc} watches from a distant hill, pleased.

fail.log: You carry the corn down and it will not grow for you, only for {npc}, who has to be called. They come, and are gracious about it.

effects.log: You send up a thank-you in smoke, a fragrant one, and {npc} sends a second plume back, in a different colour.

events.text: {npc} is found in the sky-gardens of the Will of Heaven, standing under the tree of the first sun, and says, "I think in the earliest age we were the same god. Then we split, like a seed. I have been trying to tell you for an age."

ok.log: You dispute it, point by point, and {npc} listens, and concedes the detail about the tree, and the conversation lasts a century.

fail.log: You dispute it, and {npc} produces the cracked seed they have kept, and you have no answer for that.

choices.text: Accept it, and plant the seed

effects.log: You accept it, and you and {npc} plant the seed together in the sky-garden, where no one will find it.

events.text: At the shrine on the sea-coast, a fisherman prays for a calm day and for a storm in the same breath: the man is a fool, and a faithful one. {npc}'s calm and your storm are both on the way, and arrive at the same hour.

ok.log: You win the sea for your storm, and the fisherman is dashed, then delighted, and the nets are full; {npc} lets you have it.

fail.log: You lose the sea, and {npc}'s calm falls like a sheet; the fisherman sleeps in the boat. You are ungrateful and grateful.

effects.log: You blend the storm and the calm into a long, slow swell. The fisherman has the best day of a long life and credits neither.

events.text: The hall of the Book of Fates has a new rule: any two gods with an unresolved entry may ask to read it aloud together. {npc} has put your names down, and the scribe hands you each a half of a very old page, and a candle.

ok.log: You read your half first. The words fit {npc}'s with a small, golden click, and the scribe nearly drops the candle.

fail.log: You read your half and stumble on a word of the old script; {npc} reads yours, gently, and the page goes quiet.

effects.log: You read your half in silence and hand it across. {npc} hands theirs. You each fold the other's and keep it.

events.text: There is a god of the lower mountains who has no worshippers at all, and sits on a cold stone watching the clouds. Both you and {npc} have been sending the old god offerings in secret, under assumed names, for centuries. They arrive on the same day.

choices.text: Reveal yourself to the old god

ok.log: You reveal yourself first, and the old god weeps, and offers you the only treasure left to the old god, a broken bell. {npc} arrives a moment later with a shawl.

fail.log: You reveal yourself and the old god is too proud to accept; the old god turns away, and {npc}'s offering is the one taken quietly.

effects.log: You stay hidden together, and watch the old god unwrap two gifts at once, and laugh for the first time in centuries.

events.text: A rumour goes around the Divine Realm that the God of Fate has misplaced a page of the Book, and that it bears the true result of a contest between you and {npc}. The Hall is turned out. A clerk comes up with a scrap, and is not sure.
